To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a combined PCR amplification and reverse blot hybridization method was developed for the rapid detection of bacterial genes in soil.

a combined polymerase chain reac- tion amplification and reverse hybridization assay was designed for detection of naphthalene- degrading bacteria in soil, that a lysozymesodium dodec- yl sulfate freeze-thaw method was developed to extract total nucleic acids from soil and sedi- ments, and that the assay was successfully employed to identify naphthalene-degrading bacteria in contaminated soil.
A rapid method was developed for the detection of naphthalene degradation genes from soil using a combination of lysozyme/SDS/freeze-thaw extraction, polymerase chain reaction, and reverse dot blot.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a molecular detection system for the identification of naphthalene biodegraders in soil.
the development of a molecular method that can be used to detect the presence of naphthalene catabolic genes in the environment.
the development of a rapid, sensitive, and specific molecular method for the detection of indigenous naphthalence-degrading pseudomonads in soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PCR/RDB assay described in this paper is an effective tool for the detection of indigenous naphthalen-degrading bacteria in soils.
the PCR-RDB assay developed in this study is a highly specific, sensitive, and rapid method for detecting naphthalene catabolism in environmental samples.

a combined polymerase chain rection amplification and reverse blot assay has been developed to detect naphthalene biodegrading bacteria in soil and sediments with a detection limit of 103 cfu (g of soil)−1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a molecular detection method to identify naphthalene degradation genes from soil.
a rapid and sensitive method for the direct detection of bacterial genes in soil and sediments has been developed.
the combined use of PCR amplification and a dot blot assay provides an efficient, simple, and sensitive detection method for genetic markers from soils and sediments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to develop a sensitive and specific method for detection of soil-borne genes without the need for cultivation.
a PCR-RDB assay can be used as a sensitive and specific method to detect and enumerate naphthalene- degrading Pseudomonas in soil.
the combination of PCR and reverse dot blot hybridization is a rapid and sensitive method for the direct detection of soil-borne genetic material.
